text: Vienna, 1791. Salieri poisons Mozart.
Nope. No evidence at all.
Mozart and Salieri: the poison myth.
Mozart died at 35.
After weeks of illness.
Doctors at the time blamed a fever.
Nobody knows exactly what it was.
But poison? No sign of it.
And Salieri wasn't a jealous loser.
He was the emperor's top composer.
He taught Beethoven, Schubert and Liszt.
He even taught Mozart's son.
The two of them wrote a piece together.
It was found again in 2016.
So where did the poison come from?
Gossip in Vienna, years later.
Then a play by Pushkin. Then the movie Amadeus.
A great story. Not history.
Proof Salieri poisoned Mozart: zero.
Anyway, here's Salieri with his poison.
